deployment.explain: Modal has no public REST endpoint that deploys or updates an app; deployment goes through the `modal` CLI or `modal.App.deploy()` from a Python process. The conductor therefore generates the app and the operator deploys it — it never claims to have deployed anything itself.

gpus.label: T4
gpus.notes: Turing, sm75. FP8 is memory-only here: `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` works, native FP8 GEMM does not. The cheapest card in the catalog and the only one whose AWQ verdict the sources disagree about (see `awq` in the quant matrix notes), so that verdict ships unverified rather than resolved.

gpus.label: L4
gpus.notes: Ada, sm89. The cheapest card here that can execute FP8 W8A8, because native FP8 GEMM needs sm89 or better. For an FP8 checkpoint this card is the small option; for a BF16 checkpoint it buys nothing over the A10.

gpus.label: A10
gpus.notes: Ampere GA102, sm86. `A10` is the canonical `gpu=` value; `A10G` appears in Modal's own blog and one pricing FAQ example and is not valid, so the bundle must never emit it. Maximum four per container rather than the usual eight, and no native FP8 GEMM: FP8 weights here need the Marlin weight-only path.

gpus.label: L40S
gpus.notes: Ada, sm89, native FP8 GEMM. Modal documents 48 GB; the operator measured 46 GiB usable with the same model that was measured on the RTX PRO 6000 (issue #4). Sizing uses the measured figure. Cheaper per hour than the A100-40GB.

gpus.label: A100 40GB
gpus.notes: Ampere A100, sm80. FP8 storage works (CUDA 11.8+) and native FP8 GEMM does not (sm80 < sm89), so an FP8 checkpoint runs here only through the weight-only path. Note the L40S is both cheaper and faster than this card for FP8 work.

gpus.label: A100 80GB
gpus.notes: Ampere A100, sm80, same FP8 caveat as the 40 GB variant. The card to reach for when a BF16 checkpoint needs more than 48 GiB and neither Hopper price is justified.

gpus.label: RTX PRO 6000
gpus.notes: Blackwell sm120. The `gpu=` value is hyphenated (`RTX-PRO-6000`) while the display label keeps the space. Datasheet 96 GB against 95 GiB measured usable (issue #4), which is the figure sizing uses. Native FP8 GEMM is expected on Blackwell but was not confirmed from NVIDIA in the research pass, so its FP8 weight-quantisation verdict is unverified even though its capability is sm120.

gpus.label: H100
gpus.notes: Hopper sm90, 80 GiB, always SXM on Modal. **Requesting `H100` does not pin the hardware**: Modal may quietly run the request on an H200 at no extra cost, which changes usable VRAM from 80 GiB to 141 GB. Emit `H100!` to pin it, or record the request as *requested* rather than as observed hardware. The `unavailable` free-plan flag on this row is the operator's observation on a Starter workspace, not a documented per-GPU restriction; it is recorded as such in `free_plan_source`, while the price keeps the documented provenance every other row has.

gpus.label: H200
gpus.notes: Hopper sm90, 141 GB HBM3e at 4.8 TB/s per Modal's docs. This is also the card an unpinned `H100` request may land on, so it is what actually decides the KV budget of an H100 deployment that was not pinned.

gpus.label: B200
gpus.notes: Blackwell sm100. VRAM 188 GB is the widely cited NVIDIA figure and was **not** confirmed from a primary source in the research pass, so it is marked unverified rather than presented as a datasheet fact — and sizing says so when it uses it. `B200+` is the variant that may also run on B300.

gpus.label: B300
gpus.notes: Blackwell Ultra. Requires **CUDA 13.1+**, so a CUDA-12 image will fail: the bundle generator must refuse to pair B300 with one. Modal publishes no per-card VRAM figure and the research pass found none. The guide does bound it indirectly: eight B300s reach the 2 304 GB per-container ceiling, which implies 288 GB each, but that is container arithmetic from a list that also contains 180 GB B200s, not a nameplate figure for this card — so `vram_gib` stays null rather than being fed to sizing, and sizing reports `unavailable` instead of inventing a pool. Priced and requestable; not sizeable.

quant_methods.label: Unquantised (BF16/FP16 weights)
quant_methods.notes: The checkpoint's own dtype with no quantisation. Every card in the catalog is documented as BF16-capable, including the T4, so the minimum here is Volta and nothing in the table overrides the comparison.

quant_methods.label: FP8 W8A8 (native GEMM)
quant_methods.notes: Native FP8 GEMM needs compute capability 8.9 or better, which is why the T4, the A10 and both A100 variants are documented impossibilities while the L4, L40S, H100, H200 and B200 clear the floor. The RTX PRO 6000 is sm120 and therefore expected to work, but NVIDIA support was not confirmed directly, so it is unverified rather than assumed. The online FP8 shorthands (`fp8_per_tensor`, `fp8_per_block`, `fp8_per_channel`) follow this row: same compute requirement.

quant_methods.label: FP8 weights, higher-precision activations (Marlin)
quant_methods.notes: The path that lets Ampere cards serve an FP8 checkpoint: weights stay 8-bit and the matmuls run through Marlin kernels. It is the reason `fp8` weights on an A100 is not a dead end even though native FP8 GEMM is. T4 is left unverified because the weight-only row and the Marlin row disagree about Turing.

quant_methods.label: AWQ 4-bit
quant_methods.notes: **Sources disagree about the T4.** vLLM's hardware matrix row gives AWQ a minimum of 7.5 and prints Turing as supported with a `?` for the T4; the same document's combination table says AWQ is impossible on the T4 as pre-Turing hardware. This catalog does not pick a winner: the T4 stays unverified so the operator is told to check the vendor's own startup log. B200 and RTX PRO 6000 are `?` in the matrix too, so they stay unverified rather than being upgraded by their capability.

quant_methods.label: GPTQ 4-bit
quant_methods.notes: The best-supported 4-bit path here: documented on every NVIDIA card including the T4. The two Blackwell cards are `?` in the matrix, so they are unverified rather than assumed.

quant_methods.label: AWQ 4-bit via Marlin kernels
quant_methods.notes: Faster than plain AWQ on the cards that have Marlin kernels, and documented as impossible on the T4 (no Marlin on pre-Turing). Where AWQ itself is only *unverified* on the T4, this alias is a documented no, which is exactly the kind of distinction a boolean would lose.

quant_methods.label: GPTQ 4-bit via Marlin kernels
quant_methods.notes: Same Marlin row as `awq_marlin`: documented impossible on the T4, `?` on the two Blackwell cards.

quant_methods.label: compressed-tensors checkpoints
quant_methods.notes: vLLM accepts this method, but the research pass established no per-card support figures for it — and its byte width depends on the checkpoint's own recipe. Every card therefore comes back unverified: not a refusal, a statement that nothing here is known.

quant_methods.label: INT8 W8A8 (llm-compressor)
quant_methods.notes: Turing and up in vLLM's matrix, though the T4 cell is `?` and stays unverified. Both Blackwell cards are a documented no, which is worth knowing before treating INT8 as the safe middle ground.

quant_methods.label: INT8 W4A8
quant_methods.notes: Every card is listed explicitly because the matrix marks this method `?` in the GPU columns while its own footnote says x86-CPU-only. On Modal there is no x86 CPU option, so for this catalog it is a documented no on all eleven cards — the one row where an explicit cell list beats a capability comparison.

quant_methods.label: bitsandbytes (NF4/INT8)
quant_methods.notes: Documented as working on every NVIDIA card here, Volta and up. Two caveats the operator should hear: the 0.5 bytes per parameter is the 4-bit payload and not the whole file, since scales and zeros are stored beside it; and whether this is accepted as an explicit `--quantization` value or only auto-detected from the checkpoint's `quantization_config` was not established, so the bundle prefers auto-detection.

quant_methods.label: GGUF (llama.cpp format)
quant_methods.notes: Treated separately on purpose: GGUF is a llama.cpp file format served through vLLM's GGUF path, not a native CUDA quantisation, so it does not behave like the others and its byte width depends on the file's own quantisation level (`Q4_K_M` and friends). The T4 cell is `?` in the matrix and stays unverified.

quant_methods.label: NVFP4 / MXFP4
quant_methods.notes: Blackwell only (sm100+), so everything older fails the capability comparison and is reported as unsupported. Both capable cards are `?` in the matrix and stay unverified. The online shorthands `nvfp4_per_token` and `mxfp4` follow this row.

kv_cache_dtypes.label: Auto (checkpoint dtype)
kv_cache_dtypes.notes: vLLM's default: the cache uses the model's own dtype, so a BF16 checkpoint caches in 2 bytes per element. Sizing reads the checkpoint's `torch_dtype` for this case and falls back to 2 with an assumption line when the config does not state one.

kv_cache_dtypes.label: BF16
kv_cache_dtypes.notes: Two bytes per element, no precision loss against a BF16 checkpoint. The expensive choice, and the one to compare an fp8 deployment against.

kv_cache_dtypes.label: FP16
kv_cache_dtypes.notes: Two bytes per element. Legal on every card here; rarely worth choosing over BF16.

kv_cache_dtypes.label: FP8
kv_cache_dtypes.notes: One byte per element, halving the cache against BF16 — the single biggest lever on how many tokens fit. Storage-only: it needs CUDA 11.8+ and **not** sm89, so it is legal on the T4 and the A100 even though FP8 GEMM is not. This is the dtype the operator measured both reference pools with.

kv_cache_dtypes.label: FP8 E4M3
kv_cache_dtypes.notes: The explicit spelling of the 4-bit-exponent FP8 format: one byte per element, wider range than E5M2 at the cost of mantissa precision. Same hardware rules as `fp8`.

kv_cache_dtypes.label: FP8 E5M2
kv_cache_dtypes.notes: The 5-bit-exponent variant: one byte per element, more range and less precision than E4M3. Same hardware rules as `fp8`.

notes: `free_plan` is a three-state value: `available`, `unavailable`, or `unknown`. It is `unavailable` only where that was observed (H100, spelled `H100!` on the free plan); every other card is `unknown`, which is not a synonym for `paid` and must not be rendered as one.
`source` on a card is the provenance of its price and VRAM figures; `vram_source` is the provenance of the VRAM figure alone, and is absent when the catalog has none.
`checked_at` is the date the catalog was last reconciled with the URLs in `sources`, not the date of this request.
